prompt: An intimate opaque gouache painting of an evening theater ticket counter. On the counter a small tangerine-orange paper admission ticket rests on a white cotton glove under indigo-violet booth light. The first glance goes to the tiny ticket: a single vivid warm shape with a crisp edge on the quiet cool field. Translate white fabric into pale, faintly violet lit planes, deeper blue-violet creases, a soft stitched edge and a folded cuff. Thin paper casts a narrow shadow on the cloth. Low-contrast framing of the ticket window behind; matte brush-loaded flat strokes and opaque layered paint throughout.

Relief woodcut printed on uncolored paper with one ink only, deep navy. A wave is actually cresting over a breakwater, the bright lip folding above and spilling down past the seaward barrier. Leave branching spray and broad froth wholly uninked as exposed white paper. Make distance and wetness legible with cutting alone: sparse level strokes on the far sea, broad dark angular faces and a few bright uncut-paper reflections on the wet rocks closest to us. Uneven ink transfer and tapering gouge cuts visible throughout. No other colored ink, painted white or tonal wash.

A single horizontal charcoal diptych, two adjacent narrative drawings separated by a slim blank gutter. A neighborhood bicycle repair shop that had been closed is opening for business again. Recognizably one storefront, with the same roll-up shutter, arched side window and bent wheel bracket in both views. Left: catch the mechanic physically pushing up the partly raised shutter, with a bicycle in the newly opening doorway. Right: no human figures anywhere. The shutter is now fully raised; bright swept path across dusty threshold, a working repair stand with a bicycle clamped in place and a freshly set-out tool roll just inside the open doorway. A shop visibly made ready to serve. Model both with rubbed charcoal masses, erased highlights and stumped shadows on the same paper. Absolutely no lettering, signs with writing, captions, digits, dialogue or signatures in either panel.

Draw a single two-panel black-ink comic, left to right with a narrow gutter. In both frames exactly the same lone short-haired person in a cuffed jacket sits on the same slatted rooftop bench at the same place. Repeat the parapet corner, low roof vent, distant apartment skyline and bench; same mild overcast daylight, shadow direction and weather in both, no other people. Left: an uncomfortable distance from the world, seated precariously at the very end of the bench, knees drawn inward, closed shoulders, eyes beyond the parapet; leave a conspicuous length of empty seat and isolating space. Right: the same person settles their weight into the same bench, one arm resting along its back, feet easy, face quietly enjoying the open view. Frame nearer to read the relaxed posture. Economy of pen lines and black shadow shapes. No words, captions, speech balloons, signage, symbols explaining feelings, or text of any kind.

A candid observational street sketch of the instant a shopper's paper grocery bag bursts at the BOTTOM. Compose one continuous visible action from hand to pavement: fingers still looped through the intact handles, weight pulls the kraft bag downward, the bottom seam has just split and ragged flaps hang apart. Plump mandarins clearly emerge through the open underside in a short staggered column: at least two visibly in midair with daylight beneath, while exactly one has just touched the sidewalk and meets its small contact shadow. Keep the hand, handles, opening, fruit and contact with pavement distinct in the framing. Loose searching ink lines and spare watercolor on sketch paper, street details subordinate to the falling oranges.

A side-on documentary photograph freezing a domino cascade moving from frame LEFT to frame RIGHT along one straight row on a wooden desk. Camera low, looking perpendicular to the row, enough desk surface to see the common line of feet. Read across in one continuous chain, no resets or isolated arrangements: leftmost tiles have already fallen nearly horizontal onto each other with their tops pointing right; a succession leaning to the right increases in angle toward the wavefront; at the leading edge the upper right corner of the last leaning tile is visibly touching the LEFT face of its nearly vertical neighbor; several equally spaced tiles to their right are still completely upright. Each tile pivots about its own base, close enough for its top to reach the next. Natural window light, fast shutter, sharp real contact edges, quiet background. No diagram, writing, arrows, motion trails or multiple exposures.

A quiet, unretouched-looking photograph inside an old library. There is exactly one impossible thing: a single worn, slightly open clothbound book hangs perfectly still in empty air over the hardwood aisle. Show daylight around its silhouette and an unmistakable gap underneath, away from shelves, chairs and tables. One loose leaf that has fallen from that book lies entirely flat against the floorboards directly below, its edges foreshortened with the floor. Show modest, diffuse shadow and matching side-window light on book, leaf and floor. The wooden chairs stand solidly on all their feet, the surrounding books sit ordinarily on shelves or supported stacks. Subtle wear and quiet natural tones. No other suspended objects, swirling pages, magical light or drawn motion effects.

On-location watercolor of a little fishing harbor just after the tide has drained away. A small working fishing boat now rests with its hull pressed into the exposed shiny tidal mud, slightly canted and casting a tight shadow where the keel bears on the mud. Behind the boat there is still a continuous navigable ribbon of water. Let the harbor's recent high water read in salt-darkened tide marks and wet seaweed on the quay above the mud, little runnels flowing into the channel and scattered reflective wet patches. Frame both the grounded hull and the channel beyond within the same harbor. Transparent layered washes on textured paper with loose observed edges, cool watery reflections and earth pigments; field sketch scale and immediacy.
